clue.text: Lose temper with fellow student on year out — time he gets a grip

blocks.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fellow
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate
Y is the abbreviation for year
a light that is out is off
T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written
a handle is what you grip something by

explanation.surface: A student back from a gap year is impatient for someone to get a grip on things.
explanation.walkthrough: A long chain of single letters builds the first word: fellow, student and year each shrink to one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly off the handle is an idiom for suddenly losing one's temper, like an axe-head flying loose.

clue.text: Burn Queen's flag

blocks.note: a burn is a Scottish word for a small stream
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen; the 's joins her to the flag

explanation.surface: Someone sets fire to the royal standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burn' looks like a verb about destroying the flag, but it is the Scottish noun for a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long narrow pennant or ribbon flown from a mast, a kind of flag.

clue.text: Boring first biopic with Lana Turner?

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the following word
read as one who turns, it tells you to turn the name over into a new order

blocks.note: the opening letter of biopic
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dull opening film biography about the Hollywood star Lana Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: Lana Turner was a 1940s film star; here her surname is split off as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something banal is trite and unoriginal, which is a near synonym of boring.

clue.text: Untrained soldier''s coming back, not having managed

indicators.note: something coming back travels the opposite way, so read the word upwards
having means holding, so one word is held inside the other

blocks.note: a GI is an American soldier
taken as written, to hold the next piece
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: A raw recruit is returning after failing to cope.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s after soldier stands for 'is', joining the reversal indicator; 'having' wraps the word not around the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ignorant lacks knowledge or training in a subject, so untrained is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Writer's sending copy in to the Sunday Express initially

indicators.note: initially points at the opening letters of the paper's two words
sending something in to a place puts it inside

blocks.note: the opening letters of Sunday and Express
to crib is to copy someone else's work

explanation.surface: A journalist is filing a copy of an article to a Sunday newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sunday Express is a British national newspaper; only its initials are used, wrapped round the copying word.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe is a person who writes, originally a copyist of manuscripts, now loosely any writer.

clue.text: Sausage, fried potato and fizzy drink top off time at Space Centre

indicators.note: taking the top off a down word removes its first letter
the centre of a word is its middle letter

blocks.note: a chip is a piece of fried potato
cola is a fizzy soft drink
T is the abbreviation for time
the middle letter of the five-letter word space

explanation.surface: A fry-up menu of sausage, chips and a fizzy drink, then time out at a space centre.
explanation.walkthrough: COLA loses its first letter to leave OLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipolata is a small thin sausage, the kind served at parties or with roast turkey.

clue.text: Wine cartel has broken up

indicators.note: a cartel that has broken up is scattered, so its letters fall into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A price-fixing group of wine producers has been dissolved.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red wine from Bordeaux.

clue.text: Totally calm when a couple of coppers drag doctor into prison

indicators.note: dragging someone into a place puts them inside it

blocks.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, so two of them
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
the cooler is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Police officers coolly haul a doctor off to jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The coppers are copper atoms, not police: Cu is copper's chemical symbol. AS A CUCU MB goes between COOL and ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Cool as a cucumber is an idiom for someone completely unflustered under pressure.

clue.text: Tired of chopping the garlic

indicators.note: chopping cuts things up, so the letters are cut and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook is fed up with chopping garlic.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargic means sluggish and lacking energy, the state of someone tired.

clue.text: Endlessly superficial greeting

indicators.note: without ends, the word loses its letters at both extremes

blocks.note: something superficial is shallow

explanation.surface: A perpetually insincere hello from someone shallow.
explanation.walkthrough: Both the first and last letters go.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallo is a variant spelling of hello, the everyday greeting.

clue.text: Herb free-range ducks have swallowed

indicators.note: letters set free can move about into a new order
what is swallowed ends up inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O; two ducks give two
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Free-range ducks have eaten some herbs from the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free-range' reads as one farming term, but it splits into an anagram signal and its fodder. In cricket, a duck is a score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is an aromatic herb of the mint family, much used in Italian cooking.

clue.text: Risk I'm taking for the Italian

blocks.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
per means for each, as in 'per head'
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they are taking a chance on behalf of an Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: To imperil is to put in danger, which is what to risk something means as a verb.

clue.text: Female bird returned and hit the roof

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so read the bird backwards

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: A hen bird came back and flew into the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit the roof' looks physical but is the idiom for getting angry.
explanation.definitionFit: To fume is to seethe with anger, and hitting the roof is an idiom for losing one's temper.

clue.text: A count enters into plots with hangers-on

indicators.note: whatever enters into something goes inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
to tell is an old word for to count, as a bank teller does
plots of land are building sites

explanation.surface: An aristocratic count gets involved in conspiracies alongside his entourage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' suggests a nobleman, but it is the verb meaning to tally.
explanation.definitionFit: Satellites can mean followers or dependants who cling to a more powerful person, like hangers-on.

clue.text: Fibs a little bit to come by Oriental remains

blocks.note: a whit is a tiny amount, as in 'not a whit'
E for eastern, the compass point of the Orient
something that lies somewhere remains there

explanation.surface: A few tiny lies come with the leftovers from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: White lies are small harmless untruths, the sort of minor fibs told out of politeness.

clue.text: Hurt head on a road? What pointless protective headgear!

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
without a point, the word loses a compass direction letter

blocks.note: the first letter of hurt
taken as written
Rd is the abbreviation for road
taken as written; W is the compass point west

explanation.surface: A road accident victim with a head injury wonders what use a safety helmet was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What pointless' looks like an exclamation, but W, a compass point, is dropped from what.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard hat is a rigid safety helmet worn on building sites to protect the head.

clue.text: Enormous bird on an island gets caught

blocks.note: the tit is a small songbird
taken as written
I is the abbreviation for island
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A huge bird living on an island is captured.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means of colossal size, from the Titans, the giant gods of Greek myth.

clue.text: Disturbing turn taken by Russian currency today

definitions.note: the answer is a participle, disturbed, rather than disturbing

blocks.note: the first letter of turn
the rouble is the currency of Russia
the last letter of today

explanation.surface: The Russian rouble takes an alarming turn on the markets today.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is loose: the currency follows the first letter of turn and precedes the last of today, with no word signalling either selection.
explanation.definitionFit: Troubled means worried or disturbed, close to the sense of disturbing, though the inflection differs.

clue.text: Left local team

blocks.note: somewhere local is near
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A player has quit the neighbourhood club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb, quitting the team, but it is the adjective for direction.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the nearside of a vehicle is its left side, the side nearest the kerb.

clue.text: Man United leaving place causes uncertainty

indicators.note: something leaving a place is no longer in it, so that letter goes

blocks.note: he is the pronoun for a man
U is the abbreviation for United in team names
a situation is a place or location

explanation.surface: Manchester United leaving its ground causes uncertainty among fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man United' is the football club Manchester United, but here the words split into a pronoun and an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitation is a pause from indecision, the outward sign of uncertainty.

clue.text: Add some cash for call

indicators.note: only some of the word is kept, so its tail is cut away

blocks.note: to sum is to add up
cash is money

explanation.surface: Pay a little extra to make a telephone call.
explanation.walkthrough: MONEY loses its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To summon someone is to call them to come, as a court summons a witness.

clue.text: Care about hard drive?

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: something in your care is held in trust
H is the pencil-lead abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone worries over a computer's hard drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard drive' looks like one computing term, but hard is wordplay and drive the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrust is forward push or driving force, and drive in that sense means the same.

clue.text: Hospital care includes toiletry provision

indicators.note: the words include the answer within them, spanning the gap between them

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Patient care in a hospital covers washing supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc, or talcum powder, is a toiletry dusted on the skin after bathing.

clue.text: Old king's upset and pale as ash

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read upwards

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
R, for Rex, is Latin for king
wan means pale and sickly

explanation.surface: An elderly monarch is distressed and white as ash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pale as ash' reads as a simile, but ash is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan is also called the mountain ash, a tree with red berries.

clue.text: When finally limb is exercised, I''m not sure it''s more agile

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it
a limb being exercised is moved about, so its letters move into a new order

blocks.note: the last letter of when
taken as written, to be rearranged
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone doubts whether exercising a limb really makes it more supple.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimbler is the comparative of nimble, quick and light in movement, so more agile.

clue.text: Flowers with note give some heart after bereavement

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters

blocks.note: B is a musical note
a bereavement is the loss of someone
the two middle letters of some

explanation.surface: Flowers and a card offer some comfort to the bereaved.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a sympathy bouquet with a note attached; the note is the musical letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Blossom is the mass of flowers on a tree or bush, so it can stand for flowers.

clue.text: Free toilets require key

blocks.note: loo is British slang for toilet
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Public toilets that are free to use still need a key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' suggests a door key, but it is a musical key.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose means unconfined or set at liberty, so free in that sense.

clue.text: Daughters in Eskdale contrived to run off

indicators.note: something contrived is artificially arranged, so the letters are rearranged
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter; two for the plural
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Two girls in a Cumbrian valley engineered an escape.
explanation.walkthrough: Eskdale is a valley in the English Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Skedaddle is a colloquial word meaning to run away hurriedly.
